key_insight: Skelebones turns temporally-consistent deformable Gaussians into an interpretable rig (free-form bones + a mean-curvature skeleton) so category-level non-rigid reconstructions become controllable and animatable.
problem_solved: Free-form Gaussian-based representations capture complex non-rigid surface deformations but lack an explicit kinematic structure for intuitive control, animation, and temporal coherence across frames.
method: Bones: compress temporally-consistent deformable Gaussians into free-form bone primitives that approximate non-rigid surface motion.
Skeleton: extract a Mean Curvature Skeleton from canonical Gaussians and refine it across time to produce a temporally-coherent kinematic backbone.
Scaffold–Skin rigging: bind surface geometry to the scaffold (bones + skeleton) to enable intuitive rigging and controllable animation across categories and dynamics levels.
impact: Transforms neural Gaussian reconstructions into practical, editable rigs—making animatable, category-level non-rigid models usable for editing, retargeting, and downstream learning tasks while preserving temporal consistency.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Gaussians → compressed free-form bones → mean-curvature skeleton → scaffold-skin rigging → animated output
Before/after frames: raw Gaussian reconstruction vs. rigged/skinned animation to show improved control
Overlay visualization: bones and skeleton volumes overlaid on surface geometry to highlight correspondence
Temporal consistency chart: sequence frames or a small timeline showing stable bone/skeleton positions across time (levels of dynamics)
paper_title: GaussiAnimate: Reconstruct and Rig Animatable Categories with Level of Dynamics
paper_authors: Jiaxin Wang, Dongxin Lyu, Zeyu Cai, Zhiyang Dou, Cheng Lin
